parameters.content:
## Before you activate this workflow

1. In Gmail: create a filter on `from:receipt@trainingpeaks.com` that applies a label (e.g. `TP-Subscriptions`) AND checks 'Skip the Inbox (Archive it)'. This is required -- without it, this workflow's IMAP poller and the CoachMatch workflow's poller both watch the inbox and will race on the \Seen flag, silently dropping emails at random.
2. Enable 'Show in IMAP' for that label under Gmail Settings -> Labels.
3. Set the 'Email Trigger (IMAP)' node's mailbox parameter to that label's IMAP folder name (usually just the label name).
4. Reuse the same 'IMAP account' and 'Twenty API' credentials as the other workflows.
5. `customerType` (ALL_ACCESS/PLAN_BUYER/1_1_COACHING), `leadSource` (added WEBSITE + ALL_ACCESS_SUBSCRIPTION), and `leadStatus` are all confirmed real enum values as of July 2026 (see ai-infrastructure-documentation.md). `preferredLanguage: ENGLISH` is still NOT confirmed (only SPANISH/PORTUGUESE have been seen in a real API response) -- verify on the first real English-subscriber test and fix if Twenty rejects it.
6. Members-area token generation/revocation is now real (Generate Member Token / Insert Token in Postgres / Revoke Token in Postgres) -- requires a 'Members Postgres' credential pointing at the 'members' database on the analytics-postgres container, and the schema in automation/members-area/schema.sql to already exist. The Postgres nodes' exact parameter shape is a best-effort guess -- reconfigure visually in the n8n UI if it doesn't match.
7. The 'Resend Password' webhook branch (separate trigger in this same workflow) needs its own credential check too -- same Postgres + SMTP credentials as the rest of this workflow.
8. Test with 'Listen for Test Event' before switching this Active.

parameters.query:
-- Same whitelist as the coaching insert below. This node had a bare $4,
-- which cannot violate NOT NULL but WILL store whatever arrives verbatim --
-- a literal 'UNKNOWN' or a leaked '=UNKNOWN' -- and app.py then silently
-- routes that subscriber to Spanish. Corrected 2026-08-12: garbage becomes
-- SPANISH in the column, so the stored value matches the behaviour.
INSERT INTO subscriber_tokens (twenty_person_id, email, token, preferred_language, active)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, CASE WHEN $4 IN ('SPANISH', 'ENGLISH', 'PORTUGUESE') THEN $4 ELSE 'SPANISH' END, TRUE)
ON CONFLICT (token) DO NOTHING;

## Resend Password branch

Separate webhook trigger, independent of the IMAP branches above -- Caddy proxies `POST /members/forgot-password` straight to this webhook (same rewrite pattern as /api/contact-form, see contact-form-pipeline-runbook.md).

Deliberately does not reveal whether an email is a real subscriber (always responds the same generic message) -- standard practice for forgot-password flows.

Reuses the same Postgres + SMTP credentials as the rest of this workflow -- no new secrets.

parameters.query: SELECT token, preferred_language FROM subscriber_tokens WHERE email = $1 AND active = TRUE ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, message: 'Si el email esta registrado, te enviamos la contraseña.' }) }}

## Stage 1 classifier (Aug 8, 2026)

`Filter - Is New Subscription` matches on SUBJECT ONLY, and All-Access and Private 1-1 coaching share that subject. Before this change, a Private signup ran the All-Access chain and got customerType ALL_ACCESS + a members token + the All-Access welcome email.

**Classify Product** sets productType from two explicit allowlists. **Route by Product** sends All-Access to the existing chain, Private to a Telegram, and anything unrecognised to a Telegram that writes NOTHING.

This step classifies only. Private/CoachMatch writes to Twenty come in the next step.

Home doc: `athlete-onboarding-flow.md` sections 3.1 / 3.2

conditions.rightValue: Congratulations, You Have Been Hired by a New Athlete

## Coaching athlete upsert + members access

Both coaching branches (Private via Route by Product, CoachMatch via Parse CoachMatch Hire) feed ONE normalizer, so downstream nodes have a single node name to reference.

**Update path writes conversion fields ONLY** -- name, sport, leadSource, preferredLanguage, phones and athleteLevel are left alone, because a CoachMatch athlete is normally already a lead with real data in those fields.

Home doc: `athlete-onboarding-flow.md` section 3.3

parameters.query:
-- preferred_language is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'SPANISH'. The DEFAULT does NOT
-- rescue a NULL: a default applies only when the column is ABSENT from the
-- INSERT, never when it is present and NULL. This used to read
-- NULLIF($4, 'UNKNOWN'), which produces exactly that NULL and would have
-- failed the insert -- leaving a new coaching athlete with a Twenty record
-- and a welcome email but no members-area token. Corrected 2026-08-12.
-- Whitelist rather than blacklist: any value that is not one of the three
-- real enum members becomes SPANISH, which is the same fallback app.py
-- already applies when it reads this column. NULL takes the ELSE branch too.
INSERT INTO subscriber_tokens (twenty_person_id, email, token, preferred_language, active)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, CASE WHEN $4 IN ('SPANISH', 'ENGLISH', 'PORTUGUESE') THEN $4 ELSE 'SPANISH' END, TRUE)
ON CONFLICT (token) DO NOTHING;

parameters.content:
## Duplicate-on-create catch

`Check Existing Person (Coaching)` dedupes by EMAIL only. Twenty's own duplicate detection also considers NAME -- so a hand-created or backfilled athlete stored under a different email (or none) passes the check and is then rejected on create.

This is an expected business case, not an exception, so it gets its own message instead of the generic error workflow.

Set `Create Person (Coaching)` -> Settings -> On Error -> **Continue (using error output)**, then wire its ERROR output here.

## 1:1 welcome email

**Set FORM_URL inside `Build Welcome Email` before activating.** The node throws on purpose if you don't -- better a failed run than a paying athlete receiving a dead link.

Spanish is the fallback when `preferredLanguage` is UNKNOWN (Ivan's call). EN/PT are used only when Twenty actually says so, so a known English athlete never gets a Spanish email.

Home doc: `athlete-onboarding-flow.md` section 3.4

## Welcome All-Access en 3 idiomas

Reemplaza copy que era español fijo Y que empezaba con la línea literal *"NOTE: placeholder copy -- rewrite once..."* — se enviaba al suscriptor. Nunca le llegó a nadie: no hubo altas de All-Access desde que el workflow salió, el 24/7/2026.

Sin número de planes a propósito: el catálogo se movió cuatro veces en cinco días.
